I'm 75 this year, and I've been farming these same fields for 50 years. Never went to school — can't read a word — but I know this land better than anyone with a diploma. My farm is 14 mu. Nine mu is my wheat-maize rotation, and the other five mu is cotton. My household has six mouths: me, my wife, my youngest son and his wife, and two grandchildren. My son and daughter-in-law work at the factory in Handan, so they're gone most weeks. That leaves me, my wife, and my grandson who's in middle school to do the farm work. My back isn't what it used to be, and my knees ache in the morning, so I can't carry heavy bags anymore. I mostly supervise and do the lighter jobs.

The wheat went in last October, same as always. I used seed I saved from the year before — why buy new when this variety has done fine for ten years? Before planting, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. That's about 50 jin per mu. I don't know the exact numbers in kilograms, but it's roughly a bag. The wheat is sleeping now, but come March when it greens up, I'll topdress with half a bag of urea on each mu. If it looks yellow, maybe a bit more. I'd rather put too much than too little — a bad wheat year means we don't have enough flour for the year. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once in March when it wakes up, and once at heading if the rain doesn't come. I hired Old Zhang's tractor to plow last fall, cost me some money but my back can't handle the plow anymore. I expect about 400 jin per mu, same as most years. Not great, not terrible.

For the maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we rush. Sometimes we only have five days between harvest and planting. The maize seed I always buy new — everyone knows you can't save hybrid seed, it won't grow right. I hire Old Zhang again to rotary-till quick after the wheat straw is cleared. One bag of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, and when the maize is knee-high, another half bag of urea. Summer has some rain, so I only irrigate twice unless July is very dry. I hope for 450 jin per mu, maybe 500 if the weather is kind.

The cotton on the five mu is a lot of work. I plant in late April after the last frost. I use less fertilizer than the grain — maybe half a bag of compound per mu at planting, and a little urea when it flowers. Cotton needs more spraying for bugs. I spray insecticide three or four times, and herbicide once. I water it twice — once in June if it's dry, and once in August. The picking is what kills me at my age. Three, four picks from September to October. My wife and grandson help, but it's still bending over all day. I keep thinking I should give up cotton, but the cotton money pays for my grandson's school fees. I expect about 250 jin of lint per mu.

Money is tight this year. Fertilizer prices went up again. I have about five thousand yuan I can spend on inputs, and I need to stay within that. My son sends some money home, but we need cash for my blood pressure medicine too. I'm not trying to get the highest yield in the village — I just need enough to feed my family, pay for school, and not lose money. If my neighbor Old Li uses more fertilizer, I don't follow him blindly. I use what I can afford.
